steps.note: One step, producing a proposal at Awaiting approval. Nothing posts, no credit is held and the family is told nothing until a School Admin approves it (BR-1).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. No payment on the invoice, an amount above what was received, a missing description, a student with no family code and an invoice already settled another way are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the proposal with its reason, its description and the family code it would credit, together with the audit entry or not at all. The invoice is untouched, the original payment is untouched, nothing posts to the ledger and no credit balance exists. Approving it is a separate act by a different person.

operations.name: fee.credit.raise
operations.idempotencyKey: invoice_id + amount, since one wrong charge carries one open credit proposal
operations.purpose: Raise a credit proposal against an invoice money has been received on, for the whole amount paid or part of it.

parameters.name: invoice_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, period, billed and received.

parameters.notes: An issued invoice against which money has been received (BR-2, E1).

parameters.name: amount
parameters.notes: Greater than zero and not more than what was actually received against the invoice (BR-6, E2). May be part of it, where only part of the charge was wrong (BR-11). Exactly the figure the actor states — crediting more than was paid would hand the family money the school never took.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.type: enum: Wrong amount charged | Charged to the wrong student | Duplicate charge | Concession not applied | Charge should not have been raised | Other
parameters.notes: Why the charge was wrong (BR-4). Read from what the actor stated, never chosen to fit.

parameters.name: description
parameters.notes: 20 to 500 characters. What actually went wrong (BR-4, E3). The actor's own words — money sitting on a household account has to be explainable years later.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Awaiting approval. No credit is held yet.

fields.name: amount_received
fields.description: What was actually paid against the invoice, for comparison (BR-6).

fields.name: family_code
fields.description: The household the credit would be held against, taken from the student and never chosen (BR-3).

fields.name: credit_balance_after
fields.description: What the household would hold once approved.

fields.name: children_in_household
fields.description: Every child the credit would reduce a bill for — a parent expects an overpayment for one child to count for another (BR-3).

fields.name: raised_by
fields.description: The acting user, who may not also approve it (BR-1).

errors.meaning: No money has been received against the invoice.
errors.note: Message points at cancellation instead. Crediting an unpaid charge creates a liability against money the school never took (BR-2).

errors.meaning: The amount is more than what was received.
errors.note: The message names what was received. Never reduce the figure to fit — the difference is worth checking (BR-6).

errors.meaning: No reason or description was given.
errors.note: Money held on a household account has to be explainable years later (BR-4). Ask; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The invoice has already been cancelled, credited or written off.
errors.note: The message names which and when (BR-13).

errors.meaning: The student belongs to no family code.
errors.note: The credit is held against the household, so there has to be one. Linking the student is UC-03-01, a separate act.

errors.meaning: A cash refund was requested instead of a credit.
errors.note: This raises a credit against the household; money leaves the school only through UC-04-11 (BR-10).

planningRules.rule: Never compose the description. Money sitting on a household account has to be explainable years later (BR-4), and a description a planner wrote explains what it guessed.

Never supply or round the amount. It may be all of what was paid or part of it (BR-11), and crediting more than was received hands the family money the school never took (BR-6). E2 refusing one is not a prompt to trim it.
Never use a credit where no money was received. E1 is BR-2 working — an unpaid wrong charge is cancelled, and crediting it creates a liability against money that never arrived.
Never choose the family code. It is taken from the student and never chosen (BR-3), and a credit held against the wrong household reduces the wrong family's next bill.
Never chain the approval. A credit is raised by one person and approved by another, because money returned to a household is not something one hand decides alone (BR-1).
Never offer a cash refund instead. A credit is not a refund; money leaves the school only through UC-04-11, which has its own approval (BR-10, E9).

reversal.statement: A proposal is approved or returned by the School Admin; nothing here withdraws one. Nothing has posted, no credit is held and the family has been told nothing.

intent.name: fee.credit.approve
intent.summary: Approve a credit, which posts the entry and holds the money against the household for its next bill. School Admin only, one step.
routesHere: approve the credit on this invoice

routesHere.text: ye credit manzoor kar do, family ka paisa hai
routesHere.gloss: approve this credit, it is the family's money

request.gloss: give the money back in cash

routesElsewhere.note: A credit is not a refund (BR-10).

steps.note: One step. The entry posts, the credit is held against the family code and the family is told their next bill will be smaller (BR-12).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. The acting role and the ledger posting are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the posting, the credit balance against the household and the audit entry together or not at all (E7). The invoice is never edited — its status moves to Credited and its lines are left exactly as they were (BR-5). The original payment stays in place and is never reversed, because the money did arrive and pretending otherwise breaks reconciliation against the bank (BR-7). The posting reduces income and raises a liability; it is never an expense, because the school collected the money rather than spending it (BR-9). The credit then sits until it is used and applies automatically to the next invoice for any child in the household (BR-8).

Message: "The credit could not be posted. Nothing has changed."

errors.note: Re-read the balance rather than retrying blind.

planningRules.rule: Never approve a credit the acting user raised. E4 is BR-1 working — money returned to a household is not decided by one hand.

Report which children the credit will reduce a bill for. It is held against the household, not the student (BR-3), and a parent expects an overpayment for one child to count for another — saying so is how they know what to expect.
Never describe the original payment as reversed. It stays in place because the money did arrive, and pretending otherwise breaks reconciliation against the bank (BR-7).
Never offer to return the money. An approved credit is applied to the next invoice and is not returned in cash (BR-8); a refund is UC-04-11 and normally only for a family leaving.
Report that the family has been told. They are expecting a smaller bill rather than querying it (BR-12), and a failed message means they will query it.

reversal.statement: A credit is not reversed. The entry stays and the balance is either used against future invoices or, where the family leaves with it unused, returned through fee.refund.raise under UC-04-11 — a separate approval by the Principal. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

operations.purpose: Send a credit proposal back to Accounts with the reason it was not approved.

parameters.name: credit_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No credit note matches awaiting a decision.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with student, invoice, amount and who raised it.

parameters.notes: The credit note, resolved from how the actor named it — the reference, or the student and invoice.

parameters.name: return_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required. The approver's own words — usually that the instrument is wrong, or the amount does not match what was received.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

errors.meaning: A return was recorded with no reason.
The acting user is not a School Admin.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the return reason. Often the point is that the instrument is wrong — a cancellation rather than a credit — and only the approver can say that.
Never chain a cancellation onto a return. Where no money was received the charge should be cancelled, and that is Accounts' work with its own approval (BR-2).
Never return a proposal to defer the decision. The family's money is sitting with the school either way.

reversal.statement: A return is not undone. Accounts correct the proposal and raise it again, which is a fresh proposal and a fresh decision.
